title: Community Leadership
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Invite a local leader such as a village elder or a religious leader to talk to the class. Name no politician or party.

skills.key_step: The child names community leaders (religious leaders, elders, clan leaders, the chief) and matches each to their duty.

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways of keeping safe in the community.
floor.question: Who can you go to for help if you are lost in the community?
floor.answer: any trusted adult such as a police officer, a chief or a teacher

representations: leader and duty cards to match
a visit from a local leader
steps: Say how they come to lead.
contexts: a religious leader counselling a family

board.say: What does a chief do in the community?

board.do: Write the duty beside each leader.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a leader in the community?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who helps settle problems in the village.

misconceptions.ask: Who guides people in faith and prayer?
misconceptions.repair: Match each leader to the duty on a chart.

misconceptions.ask: Can a woman be a community leader?
misconceptions.repair: Name women leaders in the community, such as a women's group chairperson or a chief.

misconceptions.ask: How does a person become a chief?
misconceptions.repair: Compare: the MCA is voted for; the chief is appointed by the government.

checks.question: Who keeps law and order in a location and links it to the government?
Are leaders only politicians?
checks.answer: No: elders, religious leaders and chiefs are leaders too

skills.key_step: The child names qualities of a good leader (honest, fair, listens, serves everyone, sets an example) and rejects strength, wealth or loudness as reasons.

floor.prerequisite: Names community leaders and their duties.
floor.question: What do elders do in a community?

representations: the class choosing a games captain
steps: Ask whether it was fair and served everyone.
Say whether people would trust the leader.
contexts: an elder hearing both sides of a quarrel
a group chairperson sharing money openly
a chief visiting a flooded village

board.do: Write: "Leader A is rich and loud. Leader B listens and is fair."
Wait for B and a reason.

misconceptions.ask: Which person would make a good leader?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which classmate you would follow and why.

misconceptions.ask: A leader is given money for the village well. What should he do?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss why trust matters to a leader.

listen_for: The one who shouts, people fear him
misconceptions.ask: Which leader is better: one who shouts at people, or one who listens and treats everyone fairly?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which leader people would bring a problem to.

misconceptions.ask: A leader gives jobs only to his relatives. Is this good leadership?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how the other families feel when only relatives get jobs.

checks.question: Give two qualities of a good leader.
checks.answer: any two of: honest, fair, listens, serves all, sets an example

checks.question: Is the richest person always the best leader?
checks.answer: No: good leaders are honest and fair
